name: Moldova
headline: Moldovans have a legal right to their medical files, but under 10% can see their data digitally and a national e-health record is still planned.

access.summary: Law 263/2005 gives patients unlimited access to their medical data and a copy of any part, but there is no national patient portal and no fixed deadline was verified. The Ministry of Health says under 10% of citizens can access their medical data digitally.
detail: Article 11 of Law 263/2005 on patient rights, as summarised by the Ombudsman, says providers must give patients unlimited access to their own medical data, results and records. A copy of any part is given in the manner set by the Ministry of Health. Fees and a deadline were not verified.
The Ministry of Health says digital access to one's own medical data is under 10%, against an EU average of 79% in a 2023 EU study. Only 25% of medical documentation is fully digitised.
A 2022 national statistics survey cited by the Ministry found one in five people said they had no access to their own medical file.

The EVO government app shows sick-leave certificates since 1 March 2026. A national electronic health record (DES) is planned for 80% of patients by 2030; the Ministry began consultations on it in April 2026.

control.summary: Patients have no tool to choose who sees their records or to check who looked at them. The Ministry of Health plans a digital consent mechanism only by the end of 2027.
detail: The Ministry's programme note says there is no clear, automated way to manage consent, which raises privacy risk. It sets a target of a digital consent mechanism for medical data use by the end of 2027, to give patients control and traceability of access.
No patient-visible access log in the primary care system SIA AMP, the hospital system SIA AMS or eReteta was found.

Law 263/2005 makes medical information confidential. The 2025 Moldova 1 report quotes an expert saying most citizens lack full control over their medical data, which is spread across public and private institutions.
The score sits in the 20 to 35 band for records handled by institutions without individual choice or an access log.

privacy.summary: Health data is a special category, and a GDPR-based law (195/2024) took effect on 23 August 2026 with fines up to 2% of turnover. In April 2026 the cyber security agency said an attack hit about 30% of data on a hospital medical platform.
detail: Under Law 133/2011, data on health, diagnosis and treatment are special categories. Processing needs consent or a listed legal ground, according to the regulator CNPDCP.

Law 195/2024 replaced Law 133/2011 on 23 August 2026. The Justice Ministry says it fully transposes the GDPR. A law firm review says fines reach MDL 2,000,000 or 2% of turnover, phased in over the first years.

In April 2026 a deputy head of the Cyber Security Agency said an attack the month before affected about 30% of data on a medical platform holding personal and payment data from regional and central hospitals.
CNPDCP has examined a complaint about a district health centre sending a patient's health data to a lawyer. The outcome and any fine were not verified.

commercial.summary: Commercial use of health data falls under the general data protection law, which since August 2026 follows the GDPR. No Moldovan rule aimed at selling health data, data brokers or health apps was verified.
detail: Health data needs consent or a specific legal ground under the data protection law, as CNPDCP explains.
Law 195/2024, in force since 23 August 2026, sets GDPR-style duties, impact assessments and breach notification, according to CNPDCP.
No CNPDCP decision on health marketing, de-identified data sales or consumer health apps was found. The score rests on the general law only.

journey.summary: National systems exist for primary care (SIA AMP), hospitals (SIA AMS), public health surveillance, sick leave and e-prescriptions, but they are not interoperable. eReteta reached 900,000 patients in two years, for state-compensated medicines only.
detail: The Ministry of Health lists SIA AMP, SIA AMS, the communicable disease surveillance system, eReteta and the sick-leave portal. It says they give partial digitalisation without full interoperability and are not integrated with MConnect, MPass or MSign.

eReteta, live nationally since April 2024, covers compensated medicines and devices. CNAM said 900,000 people, about 38% of residents, used it by March 2026, with 2,500 doctors and 3,000 pharmacists using it daily.
Since 1 March 2026 sick-leave certificates are digital only and pass automatically to employers and the social insurance fund.
Government Decision 556/2025 approved the 2025 to 2030 digital health programme. The 2026 consultations on the national record started from fragmented registers.

clinical.summary: Family doctors see an electronic file in SIA AMP and eReteta shows prescription history, but there is no national record across providers. The Ministry says the missing record limits quick access to patient history and harms clinical safety.
detail: The Ministry of Health says the lack of a functional, interoperable national record limits quick access to patient history and affects safety and continuity of care.
A family doctor told Moldova 1 in 2025 that SIA AMP gives patients registered with a family doctor an electronic file, but access is limited and sometimes hard.
eReteta lets doctors see a patient's prescribing history for compensated medicines.
Emergency access rules for an electronic record were not verified.

research.summary: Moldova has no framework for secondary use of health data and no health data access body; the Ministry targets five anonymised datasets a year by 2029. Trials need ethics review by a national committee, and an EU-aligned trials regulation was approved in October 2025.
detail: The Ministry of Health says the lack of a normative, technical and organisational framework for secondary use limits research, and existing data are not structured enough. Without a health data access body, Moldova cannot fully join the EHDS.
No individual opt-out from secondary use was found. As a non-EU candidate, Moldova is not bound by the EHDS opt-out.
A national ethics committee for clinical trials was set up in January 2016. On 8 October 2025 the government approved new rules on clinical trials of medicines, aligned with EU standards, AMDM says.
Score: base 40, plus 3 for the ethics body and 3 for statutory medical secrecy (Article 14 of the Health Protection Law, as cited by CNPDCP).

ai.summary: Law 102/2017 counts software as a medical device, but no rules for clinical AI were found. The economy minister said in May 2026 that an AI law is due by the end of 2026 as part of EU accession talks.
detail: Under Law 102/2017, a medical device includes software intended by the maker for diagnosis or therapy. Devices are sorted into risk classes I, IIa, IIb and III, AMDM says.
AI-specific rules, change control and human-oversight duties for clinical AI were not verified.
In May 2026 the Minister of Economic Development and Digitalisation told NewsMaker that AI is the last item left in that part of EU negotiations, with a deadline of the end of 2026.
